subject: business-studies
title: Liquidity Ratios
welcome_lead: Can the firm pay its bills next month? Liquidity ratios answer.
meta_desc: A-Level Ratio Analysis: current ratio and acid test.
final_note: Liquidity ratios reveal short-term survival risk in seconds.

concepts.def: Stock, debtors, cash - convertible within a year.
Inventory of raw materials, work in progress and finished goods.

walkthroughs.body_html: Current ratio = CA / CL. A retailer with high stock can show 2.0 yet still be tight on cash. Acid test = (CA - stock) / CL strips out the less-liquid item.
A current ratio around 1.5 to 2 is comfortable for most industries. Below 1 means current liabilities exceed current assets - distress likely. Above 3 suggests idle cash.
To raise the current ratio: sell slow-moving stock, chase debtors, renegotiate supplier credit. Each move has a cost - discounted stock sales, factoring fees, lost discounts.
